html:
The Spanish Armada was a fleet of about 130 ships that Spain sent to invade England in the summer of 1588. The English fleet fought it along the English Channel and beat it on 8 August off Gravelines, on the coast of today's northern France.

Philip II of Spain wanted to remove the Protestant queen Elizabeth I. She was helping the Dutch rebels against him, and English captains such as Francis Drake raided his ports. The plan was for the Armada to sail up the Channel and carry the Duke of Parma's army across from Flanders. The English ships were faster and had better long guns. For a week they could not break its tight formation. When it anchored off Calais, the English sent in eight burning ships at night, and the Spanish scattered. Next day at Gravelines the English battered them at close range. The wind then drove the Armada into the North Sea.

It had to sail home around Scotland and Ireland, and storms wrecked many ships. About a third of the fleet was lost. England stayed Protestant, and the Dutch Republic survived. Spain remained strong, but the defeat became a founding story of English sea power.
